confidence_vocabulary.exact: Direct run report, decision file, artifact metadata, or current source doc contains the stated result and reason.
confidence_vocabulary.inferred: Reason is reconstructed from prose or artifact notes, but no canonical run folder proves the full claim.
confidence_vocabulary.missing-evidence: Attempt is known, but available docs do not preserve enough evidence to state a real reason.
confidence_vocabulary.not-applicable: No failure reason is expected for this status.

attempts.name: Toy SQL SFT
attempts.evidence: execution `0.167 -> 0.833` on 6-row fixture
attempts.failure_reason: Train/eval overlap made the apparent improvement non-shippable.
attempts.lesson: The SFT loop mechanics work, but eval splits must be frozen before claiming quality.
attempts.next_action: Use only as a loop sanity check; rely on heldout SQL evals for real claims.

attempts.name: Expanded synthetic SQL SFT
attempts.lesson: The synthetic SQL adapter is the current synthetic incumbent, but joins remain weaker than single-table rows.
attempts.next_action: Keep as the synthetic incumbent until a candidate beats it on the same heldout gate.

attempts.name: Public b-mc2 v1
attempts.evidence: exact `0.344` vs T5-small `0.484`
attempts.failure_reason: The public-style dataset was too small to beat the T5-small baseline.
attempts.lesson: Public benchmark adaptation needs more coverage before tuning knobs matter.
attempts.next_action: Scale public-style rows and re-evaluate against the same exact gate.

attempts.name: Public b-mc2 v2
attempts.evidence: exact `0.031`
attempts.failure_reason: Increasing rows, rank, and steps together made the recipe worse and confounded the cause.
attempts.lesson: Do not change data volume, rank, and training length in one uncontrolled jump.
attempts.next_action: Use smaller controlled deltas with fixed eval and comparable training settings.

attempts.name: Public b-mc2 v3
attempts.evidence: exact `0.422`
attempts.failure_reason: Lower LR and fewer steps recovered quality but still missed the public baseline.
attempts.lesson: The public recipe was directionally better, but not enough for a win.
attempts.next_action: Try targeted data weighting instead of only global hyperparameter changes.

attempts.name: Public b-mc2 v4
attempts.evidence: exact `0.531` vs T5-small `0.484`
attempts.failure_reason: The public win did not preserve synthetic SQL execution behavior.
attempts.lesson: A narrow public exact-match win can still damage the incumbent specialist behavior.
attempts.next_action: Route or compose specialists instead of forcing one adapter to satisfy both gates.

attempts.name: Public v4 synthetic regression check
attempts.evidence: synthetic execution `0.240` vs incumbent `0.860`
attempts.failure_reason: Public-style training overfit schema-linking patterns that did not transfer to synthetic SQLite domains.
attempts.lesson: Every public benchmark gain needs a breadth/regression gate before packaging.
attempts.next_action: Keep public and synthetic adapters separate unless a candidate passes both gates.

attempts.name: Blended public+synthetic SFT
attempts.evidence: public `0.297`, synthetic execution `0.560`
attempts.failure_reason: Naive mixture training caused interference and output-format collapse.
attempts.lesson: Mixing domains is not automatically regularization; it can reduce both capabilities.
attempts.next_action: Use routing, data-mix search, or explicit slice gates before another blended adapter.

attempts.name: Static multi-LoRA composition
attempts.evidence: best public-pass setting still synthetic-failed
attempts.failure_reason: Fixed adapter weights produced a smooth tradeoff but no setting passed both gates.
attempts.lesson: Static composition cannot solve domain conflict when the right behavior depends on input type.
attempts.next_action: Prefer input-aware routing over global composition weights.

attempts.name: Routed public + synthetic adapters
attempts.evidence: public exact `0.531`, synthetic execution `0.860`
attempts.failure_reason: The routed artifact lacks public execution benchmarking and perf/package gates.
attempts.lesson: Routing preserves both measured slices, but artifact status still depends on public execution and performance evidence.
attempts.next_action: Add public execution gate, latency/RAM/tok-s measurement, and a package decision.

attempts.name: Hygiene SimPO/DPO
attempts.failure_reason: Ref-free SimPO update collapsed the policy and produced degenerate fenced/prose outputs.
attempts.lesson: Preference tuning needs reference anchoring, smaller updates, and composed-eval checks.
attempts.next_action: Retry with reference-anchored DPO or much lower LR/step count on the same frozen pairs.

attempts.name: SQL candidate selection
attempts.evidence: tooling and smoke exist; no model run
attempts.lesson: Highest-priority next recipe.
attempts.next_action: Run only after candidate rows are generated without leakage.

attempts.name: Offline rollout / OAPL-style SQL update
attempts.evidence: plan renderer exists; no model run
attempts.lesson: Run only after candidate-selection reward surface is clean.
attempts.next_action: Use after candidate selection proves the reward/data loop.

attempts.name: Controlled SQL LoRA rank sweep
attempts.evidence: not run
attempts.lesson: Needed to separate capacity from data/recipe confounds.
attempts.next_action: Run only after the next target/eval is frozen.

attempts.name: Qwen3-4B file-ops distilled specialist
attempts.evidence: file-ops hard gate `0.58 -> 1.00`; breadth `0.596 -> 0.423`
attempts.failure_reason: The specialist improved the narrow file-ops gate but regressed out-of-domain breadth.
attempts.lesson: The artifact is useful only with routed-only positioning; it should not be sold as a general planner.
attempts.next_action: Keep routed-only warnings prominent and add loader/pull smoke before wiring consumers.

attempts.name: Qwen3-4B ReST fused breadth recovery variant
attempts.evidence: depth `100%`, breadth `65%` vs stock breadth `60%`
attempts.failure_reason: Historical runtime and raw trace artifacts were not preserved, so the package cannot claim current latency/RAM/tok-s or a fresh qualitative review.
attempts.lesson: Existing public weights can be promoted honestly when the measured delta, routing boundary, and missing evidence are explicit.
attempts.next_action: Keep it research-only unless a product-specific target justifies a fresh heavy eval and re-distillation.

attempts.name: Qwen3-4B multibackend distilled variant
attempts.evidence: depth `100%`, breadth `31%`
attempts.failure_reason: Negative transfer damaged breadth even though depth remained high.
attempts.lesson: Multi-backend distillation can over-specialize and needs breadth gates by default.
attempts.next_action: Keep as failed comparison evidence; do not promote without a new breadth-preserving recipe.

attempts.name: VibeThinker 3B agentic distilled variant
attempts.evidence: weights preserved; current eval promotion missing
attempts.failure_reason: The weights exist, but the docs do not preserve a current factory eval proving a win.
attempts.lesson: Preserved weights are not a ship decision.
attempts.next_action: Run the factory eval gate and publish a before/after report before using it as a specialist package.

attempts.name: Apple on-device Foundation Models action-grounding probe
attempts.evidence: BFCL agentic `25%` full catalog / approximately `0%` compact; Pace planner action-grounding `13%`
attempts.failure_reason: Apple's on-device model could not ground actions well enough and its 4096-token context could not hold a real tool catalog.
attempts.lesson: Apple Foundation Models are useful as a free routing floor and intel source, not as the core capability dependency.
attempts.next_action: Keep Core ML for our own weights as an optional future battery optimization, not a model-dependency bet.

attempts.name: Pace Qwen3-0.6B planner specialists v1-v11
attempts.evidence: v11 reached train loss `0.001` but refused `0/30` held-out OOS prompts; drilldown shows Pace v9-LoRA `0%/22%/3%` and v11-LoRA `0%/15%/17%` on ambig/oos/destructive
attempts.failure_reason: The 0.6B specialists memorized surface behaviors but did not learn the planner judgment rules needed for held-out refusal and clarification.
attempts.lesson: A tiny local specialist can memorize a corpus without acquiring the product judgment capability.
attempts.next_action: Do not train v12; use larger base models or a different premise when the missing skill is judgment.

attempts.name: Pace clarify-v1 Qwen3-4B LoRA
attempts.evidence: 38 contrastive rows moved ambig only `0% -> 5%` while OOS regressed `80% -> 33%` in the retrospective; drilldown records the same attempt as `2%/40%/50%` on ambig/oos/destructive
attempts.failure_reason: Small-corpus LoRA on a competent base caused catastrophic interference across planner dimensions.
attempts.lesson: Fine-tuning a strong base on a thin behavior slice requires coverage for every dimension that must not regress.
attempts.next_action: Do not fine-tune the planner on narrow clarify rows unless the corpus also covers OOS, destructive, happy path, and breadth gates.

attempts.name: Pace two-stage ambiguity detector shim v2
attempts.evidence: ambig moved `0% -> 20%`, while OOS dropped `78% -> 55%` and destructive stayed `67%`; not shipped on top of Gemma
attempts.failure_reason: The shim improved ambiguity detection for the 4B floor but over-triggered and became unnecessary once Gemma reached the same ambig score with better OOS/destructive behavior.
attempts.lesson: Rule wrappers can expose the missing behavior, but they still need the same regression gates as model updates.
attempts.next_action: Keep as an option only if shipping the 4B footprint floor; do not stack it on the stronger Gemma path.

attempts.name: Pace reasoning-model unhappy-path drill
attempts.evidence: Qwen3-4B-Thinking scored `0%/10%/0%` and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B scored `0%/3%/0%` on ambig/oos/destructive under a 300-token cap
attempts.failure_reason: The evaluation budget was consumed by think traces, so the apparent zero scores were not a fair model-quality verdict.
attempts.lesson: Reasoning models need adequate max tokens and a stop-on-think strategy before interpreting planner scores.
attempts.next_action: Re-run with max_tokens >= 1024 and stop on `</think>` only if Gemma or the locked planner fails in production.

attempts.name: Pace Gemma-3-12B unhappy-path drill winner
attempts.evidence: Gemma-3-12B scored `22%` ambig, `82%` OOS, `77%` destructive and won all three unhappy-path dimensions in the n=130 drill
attempts.failure_reason: Gemma won the drill but ambiguity remained poor in absolute terms and the decision was later superseded by the general planner lock.
attempts.lesson: A stronger zero-shot base beat the local fine-tunes, but model-selection evidence can be superseded by later broader gates.
attempts.next_action: Keep as historical unhappy-path evidence; prefer current `PROJECT_STATUS.md`/`docs/NEXT.md` for active planner decisions.

attempts.name: Pace Qwen3.5 challenger round
attempts.evidence: Qwen3.5-9B scored `18%/97%/63%`; Qwen3.5-4B scored `15%/55%/70%` on ambig/oos/destructive; champion stood
attempts.failure_reason: Qwen3.5 improved some dimensions, especially OOS for 9B, but did not beat the stored champion across the full swap decision.
attempts.lesson: Single-dimension wins do not justify a planner swap when another required dimension regresses.
attempts.next_action: Use `scripts/eval_planner.sh` for future challengers and keep swap/no-swap verdicts tied to all required dimensions.

attempts.name: Browser Memory64 large-preset runs
attempts.evidence: larger browser presets hit Memory64 OOB; matching Node direct-export reproducer passed XL; `INITIAL_MEMORY=268435456` fixed up to XL while Behemoth still exercises growth
attempts.failure_reason: The original retries treated the OOB as a model-size problem before the matching reproducer showed a browser pthread plus SharedArrayBuffer memory-growth race.
attempts.lesson: A reproducer must match the production host and call path before it can explain a browser-only WASM failure.
attempts.next_action: Keep the higher initial memory for supported presets and only claim Behemoth after a SAB-view-aware growth path lands.

attempts.name: Browser speedup headline curve
attempts.evidence: single `9.7x` headline was replaced by a preset curve: Small `2.6x`, Medium `6.8x`, Large `9.3x`, XL `12.1x`
attempts.failure_reason: The original one-number headline made a shape-dependent performance result look like a universal property of the code.
attempts.lesson: If a performance result depends on preset size, publish the curve rather than the most convenient point.
attempts.next_action: Keep future public performance artifacts tied to config-specific tables with reproduction context.

attempts.name: Browser default corpus fix
attempts.evidence: the old default corpus was `863 bytes`; a Huge model memorized it with train loss `0.14`; default changed to TinyShakespeare at about `1.1 MB`
attempts.failure_reason: The demo was trying to prove learning with a corpus so small that memorization looked like training success.
attempts.lesson: Default data is part of the product claim; a training demo's default corpus must produce non-memorized samples.
attempts.next_action: Keep corpus defaults in the same parity review as model and optimizer defaults.

attempts.name: Browser learning-rate default drift
attempts.evidence: browser default LR was `3e-3` while Python reference used `3e-4`; training plateaued around loss `2.45` until the browser default was changed
attempts.failure_reason: Reference/kernel parity tests covered math drift but not hyperparameter default drift.
attempts.lesson: Reference defaults are part of correctness, not just documentation.
attempts.next_action: Add or keep a config-default parity check whenever browser and reference paths share a training story.

attempts.name: Browser WebGPU export serialization
attempts.evidence: a trained WebGPU run was lost because `webgpu/gpu_model.ts` had no checkpoint serialization; `exportState` was then implemented and worker plumbing updated
attempts.failure_reason: The training path could produce useful weights that the WebGPU backend could not export, and auto-cleanup destroyed a real trained artifact.
attempts.lesson: Long-running browser training is not product-complete until the smallest export path is smoke-tested before the long run.
attempts.next_action: Smoke export on a short WebGPU run before any long browser training claim.

attempts.name: Browser generation streaming and KV cache
attempts.evidence: tokens/sec counter was added, but browser generation still lacked KV cache and true token streaming; task `#72` was logged
attempts.lesson: A typewriter animation over an already-complete response is not true streaming.
attempts.next_action: Add worker protocol support for intermediate tokens and KV-cached browser generation before claiming interactive decode latency.

attempts.name: WASM backward-scratch reuse
attempts.evidence: standard `304 -> 305 ms/step`, capable `632 -> ~640 ms/step`
attempts.failure_reason: Caching backward scratch buffers removed hot-path allocations but produced no measurable speedup because compute, not malloc, was the bottleneck.
attempts.lesson: Hot-path hygiene is not the same as a performance win; measure the real step time before claiming speedup.
attempts.next_action: Keep the allocation cleanup, but do not prioritize allocator work until profiling shows allocation cost again.

attempts.name: WASM SIMD training speedup
attempts.evidence: standard `304 -> 191 ms/step`, capable `632 -> 391 ms/step`, net `1.6x` speedup
attempts.lesson: Emscripten/LLVM autovectorization was the right browser-training speed lever before hand-written kernels.
attempts.next_action: Keep SIMD enabled by default and use the WASM smoke gate to protect training correctness.

attempts.name: Browser WebGPU training loop
attempts.evidence: 24 kernel parity checks, GPU overfit gate loss `5.55 -> 0.002` in 150 steps, and headless-browser e2e passed
attempts.failure_reason: Correctness is proven, but speed is not measured because headless Chromium exposes SwiftShader software WebGPU rather than a real GPU.
attempts.lesson: GPU API correctness can be CI-proven, but performance claims require a hardware adapter measurement.
attempts.next_action: Collect the documented real-device WebGPU vs WASM-SIMD benchmark before quoting a browser GPU speedup.

attempts.name: WASM register/cache-blocked matmul
attempts.evidence: microbench `3-4x`, but end-to-end WASM training only `1.03-1.06x` after forward blocking
attempts.failure_reason: The isolated microbench overstated impact because the real WASM training workload was threaded, already SIMD-vectorized, and dominated by backward matmuls.
attempts.lesson: Optimize and report on the real workload, not only on isolated single-kernel microbenches.
attempts.next_action: Keep the bit-exact forward kernel for inference, but judge future perf work with end-to-end training and generation benches.

attempts.name: WASM backward_dA blocking
attempts.evidence: fwd+bwd-blocked reached small `90.3`, medium `317.6`, large `1057.4`, xl `1643.6`, or about `1.10-1.13x` over naive
attempts.failure_reason: The backward_dA optimization improved end-to-end training, but the remaining backward_dB path still limits the total speedup.
attempts.lesson: Training speed follows the backward-pass bottleneck; forward-only wins are capped until dA and dB are addressed.
attempts.next_action: Only continue matmul blocking if backward_dB or generation benches show enough remaining headroom.

attempts.name: Speculative-decoding heads Medusa/EAGLE smoke
attempts.evidence: baseline `232 tok/s`; Medusa 50-step `202 tok/s` at `21.7%`; Medusa 300-step `375 tok/s` at `20.8%`; EAGLE-2 50-step `200 tok/s` at `26.5%`, all bit-identical where verified
attempts.failure_reason: The heads trained and verified losslessly, but acceptance stayed far below the paper recipes because this run lacked long training, logit distillation, tree attention, and a full EAGLE transformer draft block.
attempts.lesson: Speculative heads are a valid local speed path, but the production recipe is data/training heavy rather than a quick sidecar smoke.
attempts.next_action: Revive only with self-generated data, logit-KL distillation, tree verification, and a real acceptance-rate gate.

attempts.name: MoE dense-compute smoke
attempts.evidence: Dense MLP `842 K` params loss `6.09 -> 1.76` at `55.6 step/s`; MoE 4 experts top-2 `2.42 M` params loss `5.95 -> 1.68` at `29.3 step/s`
attempts.failure_reason: The MoE architecture, save/load, sample, eval, and inspect paths work, but the current compute path runs every expert and therefore does not deliver sparse-dispatch savings.
attempts.lesson: MoE is a capacity feature until sparse gather/scatter or grouped matmul lands; it should not be marketed as a compute-saving win yet.
attempts.next_action: Return to MoE only with MLX scatter_add/grouped matmul support or a scoped custom Metal sparse-dispatch kernel.

attempts.name: CPU speedup bundle
attempts.evidence: all four items ON reached median `6.8 step/s` vs `5.0 step/s` baseline, `+36%`, with final loss `4.188-4.192` unchanged
attempts.failure_reason: The bundle produced a real host-side speedup, but QoS and compiled cosine LR were individually in the noise, prefetch stayed single-digit, and open CPU items remained.
attempts.lesson: The big win was fused accumulation inside the compiled trace; individual CPU tweaks need isolation before being credited.
attempts.next_action: Use the bundle as shipped, but keep Rust-FFI BPE, preallocated CPU buffers, and SVD-on-CPU AMX as separate future attempts.

attempts.name: Cold-start bundle
attempts.evidence: mmap saved `10-20 ms` and `25 MB` peak RSS on `demo.tinygpt`; lazy embedding deferred `262.1 KB`; package tests passed `43/43`
attempts.failure_reason: The cold-start path improved the measured demo case, but the 250 MB target file was missing, async spinner overhead added about `30 ms`, and persistent Metal pipeline caching was infeasible through public MLX-Swift APIs.
attempts.lesson: mmap and direct byte construction are good scaling levers, but large-model cold-start claims need large-model measurements.
attempts.next_action: Re-measure on a real 50-250 MB checkpoint and keep persistent Metal cache work parked unless MLX-Swift exposes pipeline descriptors.

attempts.name: Gradient checkpointing Mac training
attempts.evidence: behemoth B=4 ctx=1024 peak memory dropped `27679 MB -> 17816 MB` while step/s moved `0.4 -> 0.3`; tiny memory worsened `161 MB -> 189 MB`
attempts.failure_reason: Checkpointing recovered large-model memory but hurt small-model memory and speed, and the OOMGuard estimator still reports uncheckpointed activation projections.
attempts.lesson: Activation recompute is a scale-dependent lever; it should stay opt-in for models where memory, not step time, is the blocker.
attempts.next_action: Update memory estimation for `--grad-checkpoint` and consider selective layer checkpointing before broad default use.

attempts.name: KV cache optimization bundle
attempts.evidence: prompt-cache hot run `1.005 s -> 0.106 s`; pre-alloc decode stayed `706 -> 711 tok/s` with physical cache flat at `6.3 MB`
attempts.failure_reason: Persistent prompt cache delivered the TTFT win, but pre-alloc was kept opt-in, pre-alloc does not compose with KIVI or StreamingLLM, and some cache keying edge cases remain.
attempts.lesson: Reuse of prefilled KV is the user-visible win; cache storage policy changes need composition gates before becoming defaults.
attempts.next_action: Keep prompt-cache as the main shipped path and revisit pre-alloc defaults only after KIVI/StreamingLLM interactions are designed.

attempts.name: YOCO cache-halving smoke
attempts.evidence: huge cache at 206 tokens dropped `5.1 MB -> 2.5 MB`, while throughput moved `767 -> 676 tok/s`
attempts.failure_reason: YOCO halved decode KV cache memory, but throughput dropped at ctx=256 and HF checkpoint round-trip or production-quality YOCO weights were not proven.
attempts.lesson: YOCO is a long-context memory lever, not an immediate short-context speedup.
attempts.next_action: Treat YOCO as a long-context experiment until anchor tuning, HF round-trip, and long-context quality gates exist.

attempts.name: StreamingLLM + KIVI cache compression
attempts.evidence: StreamingLLM reduced 500-token cache `12.6 MB -> 6.4 MB`; int8 KIVI matched greedy baseline `100%` and int4 averaged `96%` prefix match
attempts.failure_reason: The cache compression worked in smoke tests, but int4 precision still used int8 storage bytes, K scales recompute every step, and no held-out perplexity gate measured quality.
attempts.lesson: KV compression can preserve greedy decode locally, but storage format and quality gates matter before making long-context claims.
attempts.next_action: Add packed int4 storage or grouped KIVI scales only after a cached-forward perplexity or trajectory-match eval exists.

attempts.name: Data-side sample packing and BPE-dropout
attempts.evidence: sample packing flattened CoV `0.582 -> 0.061`; BPE-dropout 100-step smoke stayed stable with final loss `7.382` baseline vs `7.597` dropout
attempts.failure_reason: Sample packing's histogram property was proven, but BPE-dropout was only a stability smoke and did not prove downstream generalization on this corpus.
attempts.lesson: Data-pipeline regularizers need behavioral evals, not just stable loss curves, before being treated as quality improvements.
attempts.next_action: Use sample-packing where length bias matters, and evaluate BPE-dropout on rare-word or morphology-sensitive gates before promotion.

attempts.name: MLXFast SDPA and tied-embedding audit
attempts.evidence: audit found SDPA call sites and tied-embedding build/save/load paths clean; build succeeded and sample smoke reached `603 tok/s` on demo and `261 tok/s` on mega5
attempts.lesson: The suspected SDPA mask/contiguity and tied-embedding duplication issues were not present.
attempts.next_action: Keep this as positive verification; only reopen if new SDPA call sites or untied embedding save paths are added.

attempts.name: A1 first tool-calling specialist harness
attempts.evidence: recipe and acceptance harness shipped; training run pending GPU Mac + local BFCL checkout
attempts.lesson: The four-step specialist contract is reusable, but the model claim does not exist until BFCL training/eval runs.
attempts.next_action: Run BFCL baseline, SFT, adapter eval, and +3pp gate once GPU/BFCL prerequisites are available.

attempts.name: B1 SQL eval infrastructure
attempts.evidence: `posttrainllm eval-sql` shipped and smoke-tested; training/generation originally pending GPU
attempts.failure_reason: The scoring half existed before the live SQL factory run, but the original PRD did not include trained adapter evidence.
attempts.lesson: Execution accuracy over SQLite is the right reusable gate; infra alone is not a specialist result.
attempts.next_action: Continue using eval-sql as the frozen SQL gate and attach run folders to model claims.

attempts.name: Factory run schema
attempts.evidence: `docs/factory/run-schema.md` defines the expected run folder
attempts.failure_reason: The schema exists, but real train/eval commands still need to emit every file automatically.
attempts.lesson: A schema is necessary but not sufficient; publish checks must enforce complete run folders.
attempts.next_action: Wire live train/eval commands to produce schema-complete run folders automatically.

attempts.name: SQL factory run renderer
attempts.evidence: `scripts/render_sql_factory_run.py` renders canonical SQL report artifacts
attempts.failure_reason: The renderer is a useful bridge but not yet one universal factory command.
attempts.lesson: Rendered reports made SQL publishable, but the factory still needs command-level automation.
attempts.next_action: Use the renderer until the canonical train/eval/report command can emit the same artifacts directly.

attempts.name: Public artifact registry
attempts.evidence: `docs/factory/public-artifacts.md` tracks artifacts, blockers, release state
attempts.lesson: Public artifacts and blockers are first-class.
attempts.next_action: Keep every artifact entry updated before a release push.

attempts.name: Technique registry
attempts.evidence: `docs/techniques/` distinguishes methods from recipes
attempts.failure_reason: The registry exists, but the next SQL recipe still needs validator/release enforcement before training claims.
attempts.lesson: Method names are not enough; recipes need failure mode, data, eval, slice gate, and stop rule.
attempts.next_action: Require a recipe card before any new post-training run.

attempts.name: TrainLoop-style tooling
attempts.evidence: candidate choice, slice metrics, trace review, batch plan, LoRA geometry smokes pass
attempts.failure_reason: The tools exist and pass smokes, but most recipes have not yet been trained with them.
attempts.lesson: Discipline is valuable only when enforced in every reported run.
attempts.next_action: Do not report the next SQL candidate without `slice-metrics.json` and `trace_review.md`.
